stories.title: Thousands March to Seattle Center in 'No Kings' Rally Focused on Voting
stories.dek: Marchers walked from Westlake Park to a voting fair at Seattle Center on Oct. 17 in one of dozens of No Kings events held nationwide ahead of the Nov. 3 election.
body: Thousands of people marched from downtown Seattle to Seattle Center on Saturday, Oct. 17, in a No Kings demonstration that organizers built around a voting fair rather than a traditional protest rally, according to KOMO News, KIRO 7 and FOX 13.
None of the outlets reported an official crowd estimate, and none reported arrests, clashes or counter-protesters.

The march began just after 2:15 p.m. near Westlake Park and moved north on Fourth Avenue to the International Fountain at Seattle Center, KOMO reported. There was no rally at Westlake Park; most of the day's activities took place at Seattle Center. The Seattle Department of Transportation had warned of rolling road closures downtown, MyNorthwest reported.

FOX 13 described it as the largest No Kings event in Washington that day. The station reported that the event included a display honoring 85 people who died in U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement custody.

Seattle Indivisible was among the event's organizers. Kathleen Carson, the group's president, told FOX 13 that the main goal was to turn public engagement into votes, and that voting is the first step. She urged marchers to vote early, KIRO reported.
> "This election is so important." — Kathleen Carson, Seattle Indivisible

According to FOX 13, organizers shifted the focus toward voter registration, ballot education, election protection and nonviolent civic engagement. One attendee who had been to earlier No Kings events told the station this one was less of a rally but still important.
Participants interviewed by KIRO criticized the slow release of the Epstein files, the federal immigration crackdown, the war in Iran and other policies of President Donald Trump's administration.

The events are billed as nonpartisan but are tied to No Kings marches held over the past two years by opponents of Trump's policies, MyNorthwest and the Associated Press reported. Organizers describe the movement as peaceful demonstrations asserting that power belongs to the people, KOMO reported. None of the coverage included a response from the White House or Republican officials to the Seattle event.

Similar events took place the same day in Washington, D.C., New York City, Atlanta and dozens of other communities, according to MyNorthwest and the AP. A March 28 No Kings protest in Seattle drew at least 75,000 marchers, according to the Seattle Police Department, MyNorthwest reported.

Washington's general election is Nov. 3. KIRO reported that the Secretary of State's office recommends mailing ballots as soon as possible after many ballots in the August primary were postmarked late. Drop boxes accept ballots through Election Day.

wire.headline: Ballard Light Rail Now Stuck Till 2042: Sound Transit Faces Locals Tonight at Nordic Museum
wire.blurb: Sound Transit and city officials hold a forum Monday 6-8 p.m. at the National Nordic Museum on the Ballard extension voters approved a decade ago, now not expected until 2042 amid a $34.5 billion budget gap. CEO Dow Constantine and Councilmember Dan Strauss are expected.

wire.headline: 'Hack the Planet' 90s-only rave marks a two-year anniversary at Timbre Room Oct. 23
wire.blurb: The crew behind the Trainspotting Rave throws a Hackers-themed, 90s-only all-nighter Oct. 23, 10 p.m.-2 a.m., with Riki Healing, only/hank, Slynky b2b Solanum and LSDFJ. 21+.

crime.headline: Another night of gunfire rattles the Central District
crime.blurb: 911 callers reported shots across several Central District blocks starting around 2:23 a.m. Sunday, including near 21st and E Cherry and 24th and Yesler. No injuries were reported.

crime.headline: Dangerous CO2 levels force evacuations on Ballard Ave
crime.blurb: Seattle Fire hazmat crews found dangerous carbon dioxide levels at a commercial building near the 5400 block of Ballard Ave. Nearby businesses were evacuated as a precaution until the leak was secured. No injuries were reported.

crime.headline: Car found half-sunk in Union Bay off East Montlake Park
crime.blurb: Before dawn Saturday a vehicle was found partly submerged a few feet from shore near E Shelby St and E Park Dr E. Seattle Fire rescue swimmers searched the water; how it got there was not yet known.

bnews.headline: Straight To Video booked at Slim's Last Chance on Nov. 12
bnews.factual_summary: Slim's Last Chance's Bandsintown venue calendar lists Seattle pop-punk band Straight To Video for Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026 at 8 p.m. The date is the first night of the venue's Seattle Pop Punk Fest run (Nov. 12-15), though the listing does not show the full bill.

bnews.headline: Drawn and Quartered head to Europe for 'Lord of Sacrifice' tour with Noroth
bnews.factual_summary: Seattle death metal band Drawn and Quartered is headlining a European run billed as the Lord of Sacrifice European Tour, with Noroth as support. Setlist.fm lists dates beginning 2026-10-29 at 1000FRYD in Aalborg, Denmark, followed by Groningen and Namur. The Hague's city events listing shows a stop at Musicon on 2026-11-03 and calls the band Seattle death metal veterans who began as Plague Bearer. A Bristol listing at The Gryphon on 2026-11-02 with Noroth and Mortal Filth looks like part of the same run, but it does not name the band's hometown.
